summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and recurrent tracheitis was admitted due to worsening cough, increased green sputum, and severe throat and chest pain despite being on outpatient ciprofloxacin and doxycycline. She had intermittent chills but no fever or respiratory distress. A chest X-ray showed no acute process, and sputum cultures were repeatedly contaminated. She was treated with IV vancomycin and oral ciprofloxacin based on prior MRSA and Pseudomonas infections. Her pain improved with continued use of gabapentin, oxycodone, and acetaminophen/ibuprofen. She gradually resumed oral intake and was discharged home with a plan to complete a 10-day course of IV vancomycin and oral ciprofloxacin, with follow-up arranged with pulmonology, ENT, interventional pulmonology, and infectious disease.
